title: RAYE Announces One-Night Orchestral Show at Royal Albert Hall
excerpt: RAYE will perform her second album in full with an orchestra at London's Royal Albert Hall on October 23 for a one-night concert.
body:
RAYE will perform her second album in full with an orchestra at London's Royal Albert Hall on October 23 for a one-night concert. Titled *THIS SYMPHONY MAY CONTAIN HOPE.*, the show will reimagine *THIS MUSIC MAY CONTAIN HOPE.* with the Heritage Orchestra and Flames Collective.

Rather than selecting a handful of songs for a special set, the singer plans to perform the entire record in sequence alongside her touring band. It is a fitting choice for an album arranged around four seasons, beginning in a darker place and gradually working toward the hope promised in its title. The orchestral versions will follow that complete progression rather than treating the songs as separate highlights.

There is history behind the booking. In 2023, RAYE took her debut album, *My 21st Century Blues*, to the same hall with a 50-piece orchestra and choir. The concert became *Live at the Royal Albert Hall*, a film later nominated for Best Music Film at the 2026 Grammy Awards. She returned to the format at London's O2 arena in 2024. This month's performance is not a repeat of that repertoire. She is giving her newer songs the same treatment, in the room where the earlier project began.

Her latest record, released in March, is already full of musical contrasts. Jazz and big-band passages sit alongside soul, pop and orchestral writing, while the songs deal with heartbreak, self-doubt and the possibility of recovering from both. Those shifts are part of the album's structure, not just changes in genre from track to track. Performing it straight through should let the audience hear how its separate sections fit together.

RAYE has offered a first example of what the concert might sound like. Alongside the announcement, she released a new performance of "I Will Overcome." recorded at Abbey Road Studios with the London Symphony Orchestra. The Abbey Road musicians are not the ensemble announced for the Royal Albert Hall show, but the recording puts one of the album's earliest songs into a larger orchestral setting.

[youtube:Iy2FoVeIUXs]

"I Will Overcome." comes near the beginning of the record, after its opening introduction. It is a personal song about enduring difficult moments, which makes it a natural selection from an album whose songs are deliberately connected. The new recording also gives people who cannot attend the London show a chance to hear a full-scale arrangement rather than only read about the concert plans.

The announcement follows a busy year onstage. RAYE has toured the album through the UK, Europe and North America, including multiple sold-out nights at London's O2, and is currently appearing with Bruno Mars on his North American stadium tour. The Royal Albert Hall date is a different kind of performance from those arena shows: a single night focused on one record, with orchestra and choir at the center.

Presales begin Tuesday, October 13, with registration through RAYE's official website. General tickets go on sale Thursday, October 15, at 10 a.m. UK time. The performance itself is scheduled for Friday, October 23.

When RAYE first performed at the Royal Albert Hall, *My 21st Century Blues* was still a relatively new independent release. She returns with a second album that reached No. 1 in the UK and a concert built around hearing it from beginning to end. The setting is familiar. Almost everything she will sing in it has changed.
